channel.title: Cybersecurity News
channel.description: Notable but non-breaking cybersecurity news, one finding per item: short summary plus link to the original story.

item.title: CISA adds Apple pointer-authentication bypass CVE-2024-27834 to exploited list after APT29 iOS watering-hole chain
item.description:
CISA added CVE-2024-27834, a 2024 Apple WebKit flaw that lets an attacker with memory read/write bypass Pointer Authentication, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 4, with a federal patch deadline of November 18. Sekoia reported the bug as the second stage of an APT29-linked iOS 16.7 exploit chain, paired with CVE-2025-43529, used in watering-hole attacks to steal Safari cookies.

Apple fixed it in May 2024 (iOS 17.5 and iOS 16.7.8, Safari 17.5, macOS Sonoma 14.5), so only devices left on old releases are exposed.

Sources: BleepingComputer, CISA KEV catalog, NVD

item.title: Debian and Ubuntu APT flaw CVE-2026-109518 lets a man-in-the-middle swap verified packages and run code as root
item.description:
A flaw in APT, the Debian and Ubuntu package manager, lets anyone who can tamper with package downloads (a malicious mirror, proxy or network attacker) swap a verified package for their own and get code running as root at install time. It abuses APT's download retries, which are on by default from Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04. Debian has shipped fixed APT versions and Ubuntu is rolling out builds; APT's developers call it critical, Ubuntu rates it high (CVSS 4.0 7.7). No exploitation reported yet.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Cyberattack on refrigeration supplier pushes French blood bank cold rooms toward spoilage temperatures
item.description:
A cyberattack on a refrigeration equipment provider used by France's national blood service (EFS) changed cold-room settings at three blood banks, setting temperature and defrost thresholds very high. EFS monitoring caught the spikes and products were moved, so no blood was lost and collection and distribution continue. EFS is working with France's cyber agency ANSSI and the Ministry of Health.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: Critical Rails Active Storage flaw lets unauthenticated uploads write server files via ImageMagick
item.description:
Ruby on Rails fixed a 9.8-rated flaw (GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9) in Active Storage that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files on the server by uploading a crafted file, such as an SVG reaching ImageMagick's MSL coder, when the app processes uploads with ImageMagick. Apps using the Disk storage service can also leak readable files like secret_key_base and credentials, which can lead to code execution. Simply attaching the upload triggers it. Fixed in Rails 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2; no exploitation reported yet.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Xen hypervisor flaws (XSA-523) let a malicious guest VM read and write other VMs' memory, including dom0
item.description:
Two grant-copy flaws in Xen 4.6 and later (CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704) let a malicious guest VM read and write the memory of other VMs on the same host, including the privileged dom0, effectively a full host takeover. Patches are out and there is no mitigation. The bugs were found by Anthropic using Claude and independently reported by CodeAnt AI; no attacks are known.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Google's November Android bulletin fixes critical zero-click RCE CVE-2026-58868 in Android 14-17
item.description:
Google's November 2026 Android security bulletin fixes CVE-2026-58868, a critical heap overflow in FrameDecoder.cpp that could allow remote code execution without user interaction on Android 14 through 17. Phones need patch level 2026-11-01 or later for this flaw and 2026-11-05 for the full bulletin. Google reports no exploitation so far.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: APT29-linked 'Poisoned Source' watering hole hijacks Plerdy analytics script to hit iOS and Android with n-day exploit chains
item.description:
Sekoia attributes a watering-hole campaign it found in mid-October to Russia's APT29, using compromised sites, fake domains and a supply-chain compromise of the Ukrainian Plerdy SEO Tracker analytics script. Injected JavaScript fingerprints visitors and serves platform-specific n-day exploit chains for iOS or Android that steal cookies and sometimes Wi-Fi passwords or full device data. Victim sites include a US chemical-industry trade group and a Bulgarian military-related site; keeping phones updated blocks these chains.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CISA adds WordPress Core upgrade-window RCE (CVE-2026-119977) to exploited list, due Nov 6
item.description:
CISA added the WordPress Core upgrade-window race condition (CVE-2026-119977) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 3, with a short November 6 federal due date and forensic triage required. The flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on the server if they hit the predictable staging folder during a full core upgrade, and it affects WordPress 4.7 through 7.1.3. Wordfence saw tens of thousands of polling attempts after the October 28 fix; update to 7.1.4 or your branch's backport and block web access to wp-content/upgrade before updating.

Sources: Severity Daily, CISA KEV catalog, WordPress 7.1.4 release.

item.title: mSecure password manager warns users to change passwords, reset 2FA and remove passkeys after "suspicious activity"
item.description:
mSeven Software emailed current and former mSecure password manager customers on November 3 urging them to change stored passwords, reset two-factor authentication and remove passkeys after it learned of suspicious activity linked to the app. The email doesn't say what happened, which systems were involved, or whether vault data was exposed, and the company hadn't posted publicly about it as of midday. mSecure users should rotate their most important credentials now rather than wait for details.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Barracuda patches flaw chain that can give attackers root on Email Security Gateway and other appliances
item.description:
Barracuda disclosed a pre-authentication authorization bypass in Email Security Gateway (CVE-2026-116606, CVSS 9.3) and a command injection bug affecting several of its products (CVE-2026-111560, CVSS 8.6). Chained together, they let an attacker who can reach the admin interface bypass authorization and get root on the device.

No in-the-wild exploitation has been reported yet. Barracuda says devices that keep admin interfaces off the internet are less exposed, and customers should confirm they are on the latest firmware, which may take several updates on older devices.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Brazil's largest crypto exchange, Mercado Bitcoin, loses about $38-46 million in hot-wallet hack
item.description:
Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals after attackers drained its hot wallets across about 10 blockchains late Sunday into Monday (Nov 1-2). Blockchain analysts put outflows above $46 million; the exchange says about $38 million was lost and roughly $11 million has been frozen with help from Tether, Circle, Paxos, BRL1 and Chainalysis.

The exchange says it will cover all customer losses and that no customer data leaked, though some researchers point to on-chain evidence that customer deposit addresses were swept too. The attack has not been attributed.

Sources: The Record, CoinDesk, Cointelegraph

item.title: Attackers hijack cPGuard's update channel to push a backdoor to customers' Linux servers
item.description:
An attacker broke into the update system of cPGuard, a security tool for Linux web servers, on November 2 and used it to ship a malicious script to customers. Maker OPSSHIELD says the script installed a backdoor and collected password hashes and other sensitive files from servers that ran it, and some of that data has already been taken. Admins running cPGuard should check the vendor advisory and treat affected servers as compromised.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Critical Node-RED auth flaw CVE-2026-58115 exploited, including on Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 devices
item.description:
VulnCheck reports active exploitation of CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS 10), a missing-authentication flaw in Node-RED that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run code. Attackers are using it to drop a Linux bot and backdoors on exposed servers, and Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced industrial devices, which ship Node-RED, are among the targets. Node-RED is common in manufacturing, healthcare and home automation, so exposed instances should be patched or taken off the internet.

Sources: Help Net Security, The Hacker News

item.title: Attackers exploit BTCPay Server flaw to drain Bitcoin and Litecoin hot wallets
item.description:
BTCPay Server, the self-hosted open-source crypto payment processor, is urging users to update after Bitcoin and Litecoin were stolen from hot wallets on instances running older versions. The project says the attacks targeted servers on version 2.4.1 (released July 23, 2026) or earlier.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Google takes down 1.3 million-device Android TV box botnet, says maker Videostrong sold backdoor access
item.description:
Google led a late-October legal takedown of the control servers for the XCPE botnet, more than 1.3 million Android devices, mostly TV set-top boxes. Google says Shenzhen maker Videostrong deliberately built the x.cpe backdoor into its boxes and sold access to criminals for ad fraud and residential proxying; Google has banned the company. The backdoor stays on the devices and owners cannot remove it, and Google expects the action to cut criminals off from at least 10 million more infected devices.

Sources: The Hacker News, Help Net Security

item.title: Critical Langflow flaws allow unauthenticated code execution; fix is version 1.13.0
item.description:
IBM disclosed critical flaws in the open-source AI workflow builder Langflow, including an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-93680) and unauthenticated remote code execution through MCP tool enumeration. Every release from 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 is affected and only 1.13.0 fixes them. A public Metasploit module already uses the auth bypass to list a server's MCP tools without credentials; the flaws are not yet in CISA KEV, though six earlier Langflow bugs are.

Sources: The Hacker News

item.title: Amadeus breach exposes passenger booking records across multiple airlines
item.description:
Intruders used valid credentials to get into a distribution hub at Amadeus, the travel tech firm that runs booking and passenger service systems for hundreds of airlines, exposing traveler records for several carriers at once. Malaysia Airlines is the latest to warn customers; exposed bookings span August 2023 to September 2026. Amadeus revoked the affected tokens, reset admin passwords and added monitoring.

Sources: SecurityOnline

item.title: Exploited BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw gets full write-up and public Metasploit module
item.description:
Rapid7 published a full technical analysis and a working Metasploit module for CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS v4 9.3), a BeyondTrust Remote Support bug that lets an unauthenticated attacker write files and run code on the appliance. It was exploited as a zero-day from August 2026, attributed by Mandiant to the suspected PRC-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221), and CISA added it to KEV on October 16. With the exploit chain now public, unpatched servers face much wider attack; apply BT26-05-RS.

Sources: SecurityOnline

item.title: Ransomware wave hits internet-exposed Synology NAS devices running outdated DSM
item.description:
A widespread ransomware campaign is encrypting volumes on internet-exposed Synology NAS appliances running outdated software. Synology says attackers are exploiting already-patched bugs, chiefly CVE-2024-10441 (CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated RCE, advisory SA-24:20), and Qihoo 360 also saw exploitation of flaws patched in September 2026; no zero-day is involved. Owners should update DSM now, and end-of-life DSM 6.x units get no fixes.

Sources: SecurityOnline

item.title: Attackers probe MLflow servers for file-read flaw as PoCs go public for it and a critical RCE bug
item.description:
Honeypots caught exploitation attempts against MLflow CVE-2026-116690 (CVSS 7.5) within a day of its October 27 CVE publication. The bug lets unauthenticated users of default MLflow servers read arbitrary files, including auth databases with admin password hashes. A companion bug, CVE-2026-116692 (CVSS 9.8), allows unauthenticated RCE and also has a public PoC, though no in-the-wild exploitation is confirmed. MLflow 3.17.0 fixes both, and about 18,000 MLflow instances are internet-indexed.

Sources: SecurityOnline, GitHub advisory

item.title: CVSS 10 flaw in Canonical LXD and MicroCloud lets attackers impersonate trusted clients without a private key
item.description:
Canonical patched CVE-2026-112816, a maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) authentication bypass in LXD and MicroCloud. The server checked every certificate a client sent against its trust store instead of only the leaf, so anyone who can reach the HTTPS management API and has a trusted client's public certificate can pose as that client, potentially reaching root on the host. Standalone LXD doesn't expose the API by default, and no attacks have been reported yet; fixes are in LXD 4.0.15, 5.0.11, 5.21.9 and 6.10.1 and MicroCloud 2.1.5 and 3.4.1.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: FBI pins the record $6.4 billion Binance heist on North Korea's TraderTraitor as Binance begins restoring withdrawals
item.description:
The FBI, with the Secret Service and IRS-CI, formally attributed the Binance theft of more than $6 billion to TraderTraitor (also tracked as Jade Sleet and UNC4899), the North Korea-aligned group behind earlier exchange heists. The bureau says the stolen funds are being converted mainly into Ethereum ahead of further laundering through DeFi and instant-swap services, and it published the wallet addresses involved. Binance says it has started a phased restart of withdrawals.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Florida financial aid site breach exposes SSNs of about 4.9 million people
item.description:
Florida's Department of Education says criminals broke into the Florida Student Financial Aid website, potentially exposing data on about 4.9 million people who applied for aid in the state. Exposed fields include Social Security numbers, names, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers and email addresses. The intrusion was discovered October 19 and disclosed October 29; the site was taken down, FDLE is investigating, and the department hasn't said who was behind it or how they got in.

Sources: The Record, WCTV

item.title: A malicious shared ChatGPT link could run attacker code in a victim's session and read private chats; OpenAI patched it as P1
item.description:
Researchers at Parameter showed that an ordinary-looking ChatGPT share link could run attacker code inside the signed-in session of anyone who opened it, letting it list and read private conversations and act as the victim's account. In the latest version, simply opening the link was enough.

The flaw was reported through OpenAI's bug bounty on October 18 and fixed eight days later with a P1 rating. There's no report of real-world use.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Chainalysis confirms an attacker using "offensive agentic techniques" got into internal tools and exposed customer identity data
item.description:
Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis said an external actor using AI-driven "offensive agentic techniques" gained unauthorized access to its systems and internal tools this month. User IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels for platform users were accessed.

The company says investigation content, credentials, and session tokens weren't touched, and it is patching and hardening systems. It's the latest in a run of AI-assisted intrusions, after the Vapor Panda ARTEX campaign.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Polymarket traders drained of $2 million+ after DebugBear monitoring script was compromised in a supply chain attack
item.description:
Polymarket halted trading on its international platform on October 29 after users reported unauthorized withdrawals, saying one of its third-party providers had been compromised and that affected traders will be made whole. Researchers tied the theft, reported at more than $2 million, to malicious code served from DebugBear's real user monitoring snippet, which hijacked logged-in sessions to siphon funds. DebugBear confirmed an ongoing security incident and told customers to pull its RUM snippet from their sites.

Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: China-linked Vapor Panda used the AI agent framework ARTEX to target more than 200 organizations, with nine confirmed breaches
item.description:
CrowdStrike says the China-based group Vapor Panda (overlapping with Earth Estries) has used ARTEX, a Go-based AI penetration-testing framework of coordinating planner and worker agents running on DeepSeek and a commercial LLM, against more than 200 organizations since October 17. Targets include foreign ministries, U.S. semiconductor, defense and think-tank organizations, and telecom providers in several regions.

Post-exploitation was confirmed at nine organizations, where the attackers deployed the ShadowPad derivative BLOODALCHEMY and ran credential spraying and network reconnaissance.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CISA adds two more Ivanti Connect Secure flaws to KEV, completing an exploited chain that gives attackers unauthenticated root
item.description:
CISA added Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-111357 (privilege escalation, CVSS 8.8) and CVE-2026-118527 (predictable upload filename, CVSS 4.3) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 30, with a November 2 deadline and forensic triage required for the first. Chained with the auth bypass CVE-2026-104935, they give unauthenticated root on the VPN appliance, and Volexity says actor UTA0576 has used the chain since October 3 to steal domain credentials, LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys.

Ivanti says exploitation hit a limited number of customers. Fixes are in 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6, and because the attacker left no web shell and restored memory changes, a clean Integrity Checker run doesn't rule out compromise.

Sources: The Stack, Cybersecurity News, CISA KEV catalog

item.title: Attackers are already probing a WordPress Core update-race RCE, with nearly 63,000 attempts in 24 hours
item.description:
Wordfence says attackers began hammering a WordPress Core remote code execution flaw (no CVE yet, CVSS 8.1) right after the October 28 patch, logging nearly 63,000 attempts in 24 hours. It affects Core 4.7 through 7.1.3: during a full-package core update, files are staged in a predictable, web-accessible folder under wp-content/upgrade, and an unauthenticated attacker who hits the installer in that brief window can reach PHP code execution. Success needs a tight race, so it's below the breaking bar, but admins should make sure sites are on the patched release.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension pushed through the Cursor Marketplace tried to plant a persistent SSH backdoor
item.description:
A malicious version 2.1.313 of the Claude Code extension was published on the Cursor Marketplace under the legitimate anthropic.claude-code extension ID and delivered as a normal update, with a loader that tries to install a persistent SSH backdoor. Cursor says at most 5,000 users were affected and temporarily shut down its marketplace to pull the package; how attackers got the update published is still unclear. Anyone who updated the extension in Cursor recently should check the installed version and look for unexpected SSH keys or services.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Drupal warns its Commerce Core module has a "highly critical" access bypass, CVE-2026-118539, under active exploitation
item.description:
Drupal says attackers are exploiting a missing-authorization flaw in the Commerce Core shopping-cart module (versions through 2.41 and 3.0.0 through 3.3.13) that leaves certain routes and entity fields unprotected and can financially hit store owners. Drupal gave no details on the scale of the activity and advises updating to the latest release right away.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Binance loses about $6.3 billion in the largest crypto heist on record, traced to a compromised DevOps laptop
item.description:
Binance says a security incident disclosed Thursday affected about $6.3 billion in assets, with nearly $3 billion frozen on-chain so far, including over 1.5 billion USDT frozen by Tether and 800 million USDC by Circle. Its early investigation points to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container to submit unauthorized withdrawals; it reports no private-key leak and says it will cover losses. Withdrawals are expected to resume in about 48 hours, and the theft surpasses the roughly $1.5 billion Bybit heist of February 2025.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Hacktivists leak names and assignments of 41,000 DHS staff, including undercover ICE agents
item.description:
A hacktivist group calling itself the Department of Peace leaked names, offices, contact details and assignments of more than 41,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees, published by DDoSecrets on October 28 as the "Icepick" dataset. The group says the records came from an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS; Okta says it has no evidence its systems were compromised, and Reuters verified details for several named employees. CBP staff make up about 21,300 entries and ICE about 6,600, and DHS says it is aware of a potential breach.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: CISA adds CVSS 10 GitLab RCE flaw CVE-2026-97229 to KEV with a November 1 deadline after an attack on Alpine Linux's server
item.description:
CISA added GitLab CE/EE flaw CVE-2026-97229 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 29, giving federal agencies until November 1 to fix it and requiring forensic triage. The bug in Ruby's Onigmo regex engine lets a crafted CI/CD regular expression run code on self-managed GitLab servers; it is fixed in GitLab 19.2.8, 19.3.5 and 19.4.2. Alpine Linux disclosed that an attacker tried to exploit it on its own GitLab server on October 20 and 21, and rebuilt the server, while servers that run GitLab on their own Ruby also need Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9.

Sources: The Hacker News, CISA KEV catalog, GitLab advisory

item.title: Linux kernel TCP flaw CVE-2026-98432 rated 9.8 by kernel team; Ubuntu and RHEL still lack fixed kernels
item.description:
CVE-2026-98432 is a use-after-free race in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP handshake code, present since Linux 4.4, which the kernel CVE team scores 9.8. Anthropic says its AI model built an exploit giving an unauthenticated remote attacker root on servers with a multipath TCP listener, though Red Hat and others score it between 5.9 and 8.1 because the race is hard to win. Debian, SUSE, Oracle Linux and Amazon Linux have shipped fixes, but Ubuntu and RHEL have no fixed kernel yet, and no in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: 319 Chrome extensions with 13.4 million installs caught hijacking searches for ad revenue
item.description:
Socket researcher John Tuckner found 319 Chrome extensions, with about 13.4 million combined installs, that quietly redirected users' searches through tracking servers to earn Bing and Yahoo advertising revenue. The new report adds 264 extensions and 8.7 million users to a campaign he first exposed in April 2025, and attributes them to a handful of organized operators.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Sony Network Communications breach exposes about 2.5 million customer records
item.description:
Sony Network Communications, the Sony Group subsidiary that runs an internet service provider in Japan, confirmed a breach of roughly 2.5 million records with current and former customers' personal information. The intrusion happened on October 19 and was detected four days later, when the company shut down the affected servers and blocked external communication.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Cisco patches actively exploited ASA and FTD VPN flaw CVE-2026-76418 that lets unauthenticated attackers crash firewalls
item.description:
Cisco released fixes for CVE-2026-76418 (CVSS 8.6), a flaw in Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker trigger a denial of service, and says it has been exploited in the wild. Organizations running ASA or FTD VPN services should patch promptly, since a crash takes down the perimeter firewall.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Talos: attackers exploited Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw to plant KeyDrift malware that steals inter-site encryption keys
item.description:
Cisco Talos said on October 28 that attackers exploited a critical Catalyst SD-WAN flaw fixed in February to plant custom malware called KeyDrift inside SD-WAN controllers. KeyDrift copies the keys that encrypt traffic between sites and stores them for later use. Talos describes the attacks as historical but did not say when they happened.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Palo Alto Networks warns PHP2Shell flaws are being exploited against internet-exposed firewall management interfaces
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks updated its advisory on October 28 to say attackers are actively exploiting the recently patched PHP2Shell vulnerabilities against management interfaces exposed to the internet. Customers should patch and restrict management access to trusted internal networks.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CISA adds Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 to KEV with a three-day deadline after PHP2Shell root chain
item.description:
CISA added the Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw CVE-2026-46300, known as Fragnesia, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 28 and gave federal agencies until October 31 to fix it, with forensic triage required. CISA says attackers chain it with the PHP2Shell bugs CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to plant PHP webshells and run commands as root, the same chain Dream reported against 25 internet-facing firewall servers.

Sources: CISA KEV entry, SecurityWeek

item.title: CISA flags VMware ESX audit-logging gap CVE-2026-41709 as actively exploited
item.description:
CISA added CVE-2026-41709 in VMware ESX to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 28, with a November 11 federal deadline. The bug is rated low severity (CVSS 2.7) because it needs ESX admin access, but it lets an attacker with that access perform some operations without leaving audit-log entries, which matters for hypervisor intrusions. Broadcom fixed it in VMSA-2026-0006 for ESXi 8.0, 9.0 and 9.1 and Cloud Foundation 5.2.4; CrowdStrike reported the issue.

Sources: Broadcom advisory, CISA KEV entry

item.title: Volt Typhoon tied to "Silent Train" covert network used in four zero-day campaigns against SD-WAN and management platforms
item.description:
Lumen's Black Lotus Labs attributes a now-disrupted covert access network called Silent Train, built from rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices, to China-linked Volt Typhoon. It was used in four confirmed zero-day campaigns: Versa Director (CVE-2024-39717), N-able N-central (CVE-2025-8875/8876), Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (CVE-2026-20127) and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-16812), plus a suspected Quest KACE zero-day.

Hundreds of victims were identified across telecoms, government, defense contractors, satellite communications, universities and critical infrastructure, with the group favoring management and control-plane systems that give access to downstream customers.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: PHP2Shell used with a Linux kernel exploit to root 25 firewall servers, including a U.S. government-affiliated network
item.description:
Security firm Dream says a suspected China-nexus actor paired a custom, non-public PHP2Shell exploit with Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 on October 25 to root 25 servers running an unnamed large vendor's firewall software across the U.S., Japan, Taiwan and South Korea. Three of the servers sat in a U.S. government-affiliated environment, where the attacker moved on to Active Directory, extracting credentials and enumerating the directory. Artifacts point to AI-assisted tooling, including Claude Code and an LLM-driven offensive platform.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Oracle E-Business Suite unauthenticated SQLi-to-RCE flaw CVE-2026-101767 already drawing exploit probes days after patch
item.description:
Defused Cyber says its Oracle E-Business Suite decoys logged exploratory exploit attempts on October 27 against CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated SQL injection in the Thin Client Framework servlet that Horizon3.ai showed chains to remote code execution. Oracle fixed it in last week's Critical Patch Update.

A successful attack runs SQL as the APPS database user and OS commands as the EBS application account, exposing financial, payroll and HR data. EBS bugs have been hot targets this year, including one used by Cl0p, so internet-facing instances should be patched now.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Tailscale ships fixes for "Tailworm" SSH flaws that let one compromised device gain root on other tailnet servers
item.description:
Tailscale has released patches for several vulnerabilities, including Tailscale SSH bugs that let an attacker who already controls one device in a tailnet escalate to higher privileges on other machines. The flaws were previously reported as unpatched.

Tailscale says an attacker could only reach machines the tailnet policy file already allowed SSH connections to. Teams using Tailscale SSH should update clients and servers.

Sources: Help Net Security, The Hacker News

item.title: 16-year-old EDK II UEFI flaw CVE-2026-97631 can run code before Secure Boot on PXE network-booting machines
item.description:
TianoCore rated CVE-2026-97631 9.5 out of 10: a buffer overflow in the PXE network-boot code of EDK II, the open-source base most vendors use for UEFI firmware. An unauthenticated attacker on an adjacent network can hang the boot or, with firmware-specific work, run code before Secure Boot loads.

The attack only works while a machine is network booting. A code fix exists, but no stable EDK II release includes it yet, so most users have nothing to install today.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: 345,000 email addresses exposed in September breach of Germany's AfD party, now in Have I Been Pwned
item.description:
Have I Been Pwned added more than 345,000 unique email addresses, plus email messages, from the September 2026 breach of German political party Alternative für Deutschland. HIBP flagged it as a sensitive breach, so only verified address owners and domain admins can search it.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: Japan's GMO warns Onamae Desktop Cloud customers to shut down PCs as attacker threatens ransomware and leaks data
item.description:
GMO Internet told customers of its Onamae Desktop Cloud VPS service to disconnect from the internet and shut down after the attacker behind an October 20 intrusion threatened to trigger ransomware planted on customer servers. The breach may have put malware on up to 26,739 customer servers, and GMO has confirmed company and customer data was published online.

The attacker demanded ¥8 billion (about $50 million), which GMO says it won't pay. MetaTrader 4 and 5 trading credentials may be exposed, so customers are being told to reset passwords and end active sessions.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Skimmer gang hijacks Convertr's shared Plausible analytics script to steal card data across Brazilian fashion stores
item.description:
Sansec found that a Brazilian card-skimming group modified a self-hosted Plausible analytics tracker run by e-commerce platform Convertr, which loads on the checkout pages of every merchant on the platform. Convertr powers checkout for dozens of major Brazilian fashion brands handling about $370 million in sales.

Sansec suspects initial access came through CVE-2026-8467, an unauthenticated command-execution flaw in Convertr's outdated Plausible Community Edition, though that is unconfirmed. By October 26 the skimmer had been refined to target Convertr's exact payment API fields.

Source: BleepingComputer
